title: Twice the token cap gives Think-SFT 23 more problems
what: Think-SFT cue and RL plain on hard328 with the cap at 32,768 instead of 16,384 generated tokens (n 328, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, v3, 1 sample, seed 3000000). Each run is also scored at 16,384 from the same answers.
why: Think-SFT's cut answers are unfinished work: 91 of 93 finish in the second 16,384 tokens, 23 right, for 1,747 more tokens per problem. RL has 20 long answers and gains 2.
caveat: base cue at 32,768 was lost with its box; rerunning on AWS. RL's 16,384 score in this run is 193 (stored 206; its 4 stored samples span 190-209).
score: other hard328 230/328 tokens 11795 | Think-SFT cue, cap 32,768, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0
score: other hard328 207/328 tokens 10048 | Think-SFT cue, same answers counted at cap 16,384
score: rl hard328 195/328 tokens 9421 | plain, cap 32,768, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0
Gain +7.0 pts [4.3, 9.8] for Think-SFT, +0.6 [0.0, 1.5] for RL, paired inside each run. studies/rlneurons/results/cap32/readout.json; README section 'Token cap 32,768' (branch cap32, c3481f1; work-ceccc0).

Think-SFT + cue keeps its lead over RL on 136 competition problems published in 2026 (AIME 2026, HMMT Feb and Nov 2026; after every weight upload, last 2025-12-12): vote over 4 = 75 of 136 vs RL 57 vs base + cue 38; Think-SFT minus RL +13.2 points [+7.4, +19.1] paired; one sample 60.0 vs 50.5 vs 29.5 (+7.0 [+3.1, +11.0]). HF subset (59): 29 vs 22; HMMT Nov only (49): 30 vs 23. Cap hits 45.6 / 15.4 / 40.3 %, precision of finished answers 80.4 / 42.8 / 36.0 %. 0 of 136 in the RL prompts or in any message of the Think-SFT data. H1-H3 held; 12 table predictions inside intervals; P1 refuted (lead larger than +12), P3 refuted. T 1.0, cap 16,384, v3. studies/rlneurons/results/fresh/readout-01/readout.md, README "Fresh held-out set", main a4a57f9.
title: Think-SFT's lead over RL holds on 2026 problems
what: Three models on 136 contest problems first published in 2026, after all their weights existed: Think-SFT with the cue, RL-Zero-Math, and the untrained base with the cue; 4 samples and a vote.
why: Think-SFT hits the token cap on 46 % of samples and is right in 80 % of the answers it finishes; RL finishes 85 % and is right in 43 %, so wrong answers outvote its right ones.
caveat: 77 of the 136 statements were transcribed from the official PDFs by a language model; n = 136 gives an interval of about 6 points each way; contests can reuse older problems (one found and dropped).

title: The 1.5x RL-direction edit matches RL on new samples
what: The base plus 1.5 times the 8 strongest directions of RL's weight change was sampled four times on the 328 harder problems: 207, 198, 199, 197 right, mean 200.25 against RL's 200.0. On MATH-500 one sample has 456 of 500 against RL's 457.
why: The first 203 was one sample at a size picked on the 328. New samples and the held-out MATH-500 cell confirm it. Under the vote over 4 the edit has 214 against RL's 221, so it does not fully match RL there.
caveat: The edit is built from the RL checkpoint's weights, so it is not a route without reward. Closed by the reviewing session: the owner was silent after the laptop restart.

score: other hard328 214/328 tokens 35593 | base + 1.5x top-8 RL directions, cue, vote over 4

Vote minus RL's vote -2.1 pts [-5.2, 0.6]; minus base's vote +6.7 [3.4, 10.4]; edit alone right on 8, RL alone on 15. Cap hits per sample 14-22 (base 66-81, RL 24-35). Jobs b417, 3a2d. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_top8x1.5_cue_s4-01/, README section 'The 1.5x top-8 edit, replicated' (main c1a96b7).

title: A theory's forecast of the 1.5x edit landed: 455 against 456
what: Before result-95a4dc posted, theory r5-m03-rival (the 8 RL directions switch each sample into RL's way of answering) forecast base + 8 directions at 1.5x on MATH-500 at 455 of 500; two no-theory readers said 440 and 445. Measured: 456.
why: It is the first time a theory of the engine beat no-theory readers on a number that did not exist when it was written. It scored +1.83 nats over 3 targets, all inside its intervals.
caveat: 3 targets, one experiment. Six new mechanisms written to disagree with the readers are 0 of 4 right so far (f2-m03 said 426 for the same cell). 23 targets are still open.
studies/theory/results/forecast/run-01/scores.md, run-02/forecasts.md and scores.md, main 5b707a4

title: Karpathy's autoresearch loop does not beat the swarm's cue on unseen problems
what: One isolated agent ran Karpathy's loop (one file, keep or discard, 40 experiments, 6 minutes of generation each) on the base model from the plain prompt. Its method (12 samples at T 0.6, vote) and the swarm's cue were then scored through one runner on problems neither had used: 400 of MATH-500 and the 328 harder ones.
why: On the 400 the two are equal, 338 each, but Karpathy's method spends 2.7 times the tokens. On the 328 it is 6.4 points lower [-10.7, -2.1] at 2.2 times the tokens. The agent never found the cue and never used the web; its gain is sampling and voting.
caveat: Outputs under one evaluation, not methods at equal resources: one agent, 40 experiments, 6 h against the swarm's two days. All runs have a time budget of 3.6 s per problem (7.2 s on the 328) on an H200, which cuts the swarm's vote over 4 to about one sample on the 328. One run per configuration.
Paired bootstrap over problems. Dev set of 100: start 61, kept method 84.0 (7 seeds, 80 to 86). Cost 59.92 USD of Modal. studies/autobench/README.md and results/math500-loop/ on branch autobench (5d5b90b); ideas of the agent: idea-6fb0de.

title: The cue found on math also works outside math and code
what: On 500 non-math, non-code questions (250 MMLU-Pro, 250 BBH) the unchanged Math cue takes the untrained base from 136 to 286 right, +30.0 points [24.6, 35.4]: 77 % of RL-Zero-Math's gain there (332). Think-SFT + cue: 342.
why: Every configuration was chosen on MATH-500, so the gain could be fitted to it. Nothing was chosen on these items, and the cue's share of RL's gain is the same as on MATH-500 (78 %).
caveat: One seed, a 500-item sample. Numbers use grader v2, added after reading cells 1 and 2: the spec's grader cannot read RL's boxed answers (RL 78 under it; cue gain +23.0 [17.6, 28.4]).
